newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt govt bank securitising debt of state firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt govt bank securitising debt of state firm.

text.p: Egypt's state-owned Banque Misr said it was securitising the debts of public-sector construction firm Arab Contractors by issuing bonds worth about 500 million pounds ($147 million) which will be offered to the public.
Vice Chairman Baha Helmy told reporters Banque Misr had also contacted state-run National Bank of Egypt and Banque du Caire to raise the value of the bonds issued to 600 million pounds.
He said the bonds would be issued as soon as the bank decided on an attractive yield but he did not specify a date.

Helmy refused to say how much Arab Contractors owed the bank but the firm said in a financial statement that its loans and overdrafts had risen to 2.088 billion pounds in the financial year ending June 1996 from 2.076 billion in the previous year.
The company also said it was owed 3.094 billion in 1996 compared to 2.909 billion in 1995 and that it owed creditors 1.464 billion pounds compared to 1.208 billion in 1995.
